# 02-upgrade-all-projects: Upgrade the solution to .NET 10

Retarget `StarWarsTopTrumps.Engine`, `StarWarsTopTrumps.Tests`, and `StarWarsTopTrumps.UI` from `net8.0` to `net10.0` together. Resolve the two packages the assessment marks incompatible inline, update the UI project's `Newtonsoft.Json` recommendation from 13.0.3 to 13.0.4, and investigate the `UseExceptionHandler(IApplicationBuilder, string)` behavioral-change finding so exception handling remains intentional. The assessment reports no binary- or source-incompatible APIs; use its project and package reports as research starting points rather than duplicating package detail here.

## Scope Inventory
- **Projects**: Engine (no package references; referenced by UI and Tests), Tests (four package references and a project reference to Engine), and UI (three package references and a project reference to Engine). All are SDK-style and define `TargetFramework` directly in their `.csproj` files.
- **Distinct concerns**: Retarget all three projects atomically; update UI package versions; preserve the UI exception handler behavior; validate C# 14 compiler compatibility as the TFM default changes from C# 12.
- **Package findings**: UI `Azure.Identity` 1.13.0 is flagged because it depends on a deprecated MSAL version; assessment recommends 1.21.0. UI `Microsoft.Azure.SignalR` 1.28.0 is deprecated due to vulnerable dependencies in older versions; assessment recommends 1.34.0. NuGet version lookup confirms both recommendations are compatible with `net10.0`. UI `Newtonsoft.Json` 13.0.3 has a recommended update to 13.0.4, also compatible with `net10.0`; Tests uses Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.1 and the assessment marks it compatible.
- **API finding**: `Startup.Configure` calls `app.UseExceptionHandler("/Error")`. The reported .NET 10 behavior concerns suppression of exception diagnostics when an `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns true; no such handler was found in the app, so keep the existing path-based handler unless validation reveals a behavior change.
- **C# compatibility scan**: Projects currently default to C# 12 and will default to C# 14 on `net10.0`. Searches found no C# 14 `field`/`extension`/`scoped` identifier collisions, `params` arrays, `lock` statements, or searched null-conditional-assignment/Span-reverse patterns. No `.editorconfig` is present. Avoid unrelated syntax refactoring; compilation is the compatibility check.
- **Strategy**: All-at-Once, so do not split work by project or dependency tier. Restore/build using the installed .NET 10 SDK; package definitions are direct project references, with no central package management reported.

**Done when**: All three projects target `net10.0`; incompatible package findings are resolved for .NET 10; the recommended Newtonsoft.Json update is applied; and the exception-handler behavior is preserved or deliberately updated.
